coverage.assessment: The chain survives intact: the Inspector Brown deception is stated, the photograph is lost, and the move to the Ritz follows. Whittington and the coincidence law form clue one. The Rita reasoning ties survival to the gang's knowledge. Carter's list answers Tuppence's questions, and Mrs. Keith is first of seven. The flag-tray cut takes 'eating the flags' with it, as authorized, and leaves no residue.

Tuppence withdraws at The Laurels and waits at the turn at South Audley, then hides by the lift. Only Whittington is recognized. Cutting 'just off Park Lane' and 'second floor' does not break the stairs and lift geography.
Turn-taking is clear throughout. The cut 'You heard?' exchange removes an explicit cue that Tuppence overheard the confirmation, and it removes the pair's mutual rejoicing.

'I admit it's only a chance' is kept. The restored 'more likely to have been a woman' and 'I don't see that at all' frame the shadower as conjecture. 'Four more blanks' is consistent with the count of seven names.
The veil-drawing opening and its irony survive. Nothing foreshadows Brown's identity or any other meaning of Marguerite.

The union joke, 'Proceed, O Sherlock!', 'old bean', 'moles in the dark' and 'Ha ha!' all remain. Some mutual-deflation banter is thinned: 'zero for modesty' is gone, and so is Tuppence's 'I can do it too' parody.
The irony of Brown not having 'done us to death', just before Whittington appears, is preserved. The 'Just as though we didn't count' exchange survives.
All three are intact. Marguerite/Rita is explicit locally and echoed in 018. Rita is linked to Whittington's outburst in 003 and 013. Carter's list answers the promise made in 006.

findings.claim: The revision removes 'You heard?' / 'Yes. Oh, Tommy!' / 'I know, old thing. I feel the same.' Tommy now descends and Tuppence immediately cries out. Nothing confirms that she overheard, and the mutual joy is reduced to a single exclamation.
findings.counterevidence: Tuppence's line 'so lovely to think of things--and then for them really to happen!' implies she heard. Her later grip on his arm also keeps physical closeness.

Hardly able to contain his excitement, Tommy hurried down the stairs. Tuppence was waiting at the angle of the turn.

findings.minimal_repair: Restore the first-draft three lines (about 20 words) before Tuppence's exclamation.
findings.reader_effect: The planned 'They rejoice' beat becomes one-sided. The affectionate 'old thing' is lost, which weakens the comic warmth before the sudden menace.
findings.title: Shared rejoicing and 'You heard?' cue cut

findings.claim: In the source, Tuppence parodies Tommy's 'literary' sentence: 'wreaked vengeance upon us. (You see, I can do it too.) We pass on our way unscathed.' Both drafts reduce this to 'But it certainly is queer.' That leaves 'it' to be inferred, and her answering parody is lost.
findings.counterevidence: Tommy's preceding sentence makes the referent inferable. The core irony of V4 and 'moles in the dark' is intact.

evidence.quote: (You see, I can do it too.) We pass on our way unscathed.
You’re really more conceited than I am--with less excuse! But it certainly is queer.

findings.plan_relation: Optional tradeoff within the protected banter. The plan stresses that the banter's irony must remain.
findings.reader_effect: The banter loses its two-sided parody of formal speech, a named feature of the voice. The line also reads slightly elliptical.
findings.title: Tuppence's mock-literary echo elided to a vague 'queer'

findings.claim: The first draft already dropped 'How's that for clever little Tuppence?' but kept Tommy's 'Full marks for industry, zero for modesty.' The revision cuts that retort as well, leaving the flat 'Is there a 'Rita' on the list?'
findings.counterevidence: 'Proceed, O Sherlock!' and 'You're really more conceited than I am' still carry mutual teasing.

findings.minimal_repair: Restore 'Full marks for industry, zero for modesty.' (seven words) before the question.
findings.plan_relation: Optional trimming, not itemized in the plan.
findings.reader_effect: The voice profile's habit of the pair deflating each other's vanity is reduced at this point. The Laurels exchange still preserves the reverse case, Tommy's smugness conceded by Tuppence.
findings.title: Deflation of Tuppence's vanity trimmed away

strengths: The revision restores 'And it's more likely to have been a woman than a man----' / 'I don't see that at all.' This keeps Tuppence's 'absolutely certain' as a disputed intuition rather than an established fact, as the plan's risk note requires.
The flag-tray idea and 'eating the flags' are cut together, as authorized, and Tommy's practical objection is reattributed cleanly with no dangling residue.
The Laurels ruse keeps the servant's cryptic 'about the gas' line, Tommy's 'Child's play to the masculine mind' and Tuppence's concession.
The comic-to-menace turn is intact: 'Ha ha!' is followed by the Marguerite confirmation, Tuppence's delight, the lift shadow and the short closing cliffhanger (V8).
summary: The revision is coherent and faithful in structure. All eight verbatim anchors survive. All three dependencies are intact in both endpoints. The revision improves on the first draft by restoring Tommy's objection, which keeps Tuppence's woman-shadower theory framed as her guess. Its main new cost is the cut of the brief 'You heard?' exchange, which shrinks the planned shared rejoicing to Tuppence's single cry. Smaller voice losses are Tuppence's mock-literary echo, already elided in the first draft, and the 'zero for modesty' deflation, which the revision cut. None of these breaks causality or misleads.
